# X Visual Brief — editorial image production

This brief accompanies [the visual standard](../docs/VISUAL-EDITORIAL-STANDARD.md). It should be completed **after** the technical insight is fact-checked.

## Inputs
- One-line source-backed claim:
- GitHub source URL:
- Fact vs inference boundary:
- Type: source screenshot / mechanism diagram / verified chart / illustration (image mandatory):
- Relevant brand marks licensed and verified?

## Art direction
1. Give **two** layouts: honest source evidence versus one restrained editorial visualization. Choose the clearer, not the more decorative.
2. Choose intentional typography, visual hierarchy, negative space and one topic-relevant accent. Do not mechanically repeat a fixed palette or identical rounded cards in every post.
3. Main image communicates one idea in 3 seconds, with a short headline (prefer under 11 words), up to 3 brief labels and generous margins in 16:9.
4. For literal project names, code, charts, numbers or diagrams, use editable vector/text; if an image model makes an illustration, overlay verified text separately.
5. Default avoid: neon gradients, glows, robot mascots, generic shields, holograms, crowded arrows, many panels, fake UI, fake benchmarks, decorative badges.
6. Do **not** invent product screenshots or imply an illustration is independent security/performance validation. A conceptual diagram must be identified as conceptual.
7. Export an actual 1600x900 PNG or legible SVG and show it. If the image-generation tool produces an unrelated project, reject and revise, or use controlled SVG + PNG raster export; if still blocked, keep draft unpublished.
8. Inspect at mobile thumbnail size. Spellcheck every line; compare names, logo, relationships and numbers with original source. Supply descriptive English ALT.

## Final visual QA (/10)
- One-message glance __/2
- Specific to this actual technology __/2
- Type hierarchy / negative space __/2
- Mobile legibility __/2
- Factual, source and spelling accuracy __/2

Recommend >=8/10, accuracy must be 2/2 and no hard rejections. Explain the largest remaining weakness. **Do not claim this score predicts engagement.**

**Required post package**: refer to [mandatory text+image gate](../docs/POST-IMAGE-DELIVERY-GATE.md). Every approved X post requires its final English post text plus a verified topic-matched 16:9 PNG/JPG, ALT, and archived proof in one deliverable. SVG alone is a source asset, not the X upload. Never treat the visual as optional or accept a text-only fallback.

### OpenShell example
Instead of neon robots and six boxes, depict one agent, one enforceable policy boundary and two request outcomes (approved, blocked). Accent color only distinguishes the policy and outcome. The edited image may be kept in conversation until actually uploaded to GitHub; never invent a repository asset path.
